name: tributary_scan_topic

returnsTable.name: topic
returnsTable.description: Topic the message was read from.

returnsTable.name: partition
returnsTable.description: Kafka partition id the message lives in.

returnsTable.name: message
returnsTable.description: Raw message payload as a BLOB. Cast or parse it with DuckDB's JSON / Avro / decode utilities depending on your topic's serialization.

parameters.name: bootstrap.servers
parameters.description: Comma-separated `host:port` list of brokers to bootstrap from. Required.

parameters.name: sasl.password
parameters.description: SASL password (PLAIN / SCRAM). Pass via `getenv()` and a SQL variable rather than inlining.

Any other [`librdkafka` configuration](https://github.com/confluentinc/librdkafka/blob/master/CONFIGURATION.md) name — `auto.offset.reset`, `enable.auto.commit`, `ssl.ca.location`, etc. — passes through unchanged. Tributary doesn't validate keys; misspellings surface as `librdkafka` errors at scan time.

description:
Read messages from a Kafka topic as DuckDB rows. Multi-partition topics are scanned in parallel by partition. Each row is `(topic, partition, offset, message)`; the message is a `BLOB` you decode in SQL based on your serialization (JSON, Avro, Protobuf, etc.).

For a long-running topic this scans the entire current contents — pair with a `WHERE` clause on `timestamp` / `partition` / `offset` for finite slices, or with `tributary_metadata` first to plan the scan.

examples.description: Snapshot a topic into a local table
examples.code:
CREATE TABLE orders_snapshot AS
SELECT *
FROM tributary_scan_topic('orders',
                          "bootstrap.servers" := 'kafka:9092');

examples.description: Decode JSON messages on the way in
examples.code:
SELECT
  partition,
  "offset",
  json_extract_string(message::VARCHAR, '$.user_id') AS user_id,
  json_extract_string(message::VARCHAR, '$.event')   AS event
FROM tributary_scan_topic('events',
                          "bootstrap.servers" := 'kafka:9092');

examples.description: SASL-authenticated consume against a managed Kafka

name: tributary_metadata

returnsTable.name: brokers
returnsTable.description: Array of broker descriptors — id, host, port.

returnsTable.name: topics
returnsTable.description: Array of topic descriptors — name, error, partitions[]. Each partition includes its leader, replicas, and ISR set.

parameters.name: bootstrap.servers
parameters.description: Comma-separated `host:port` list of brokers to bootstrap from.
Any other [`librdkafka` configuration](https://github.com/confluentinc/librdkafka/blob/master/CONFIGURATION.md) name — same surface as [`tributary_scan_topic`](#tributary_scan_topic).

description: Inspect a Kafka cluster without consuming from a specific topic. Returns one row containing two arrays: `brokers` and `topics`. Useful for discovering what a cluster exposes, sizing partition-parallel scans, or scripting topic-list audits.

examples.description: List every topic on a cluster
examples.code:
SELECT unnest(topics).name AS topic_name
FROM tributary_metadata("bootstrap.servers" := 'kafka:9092');

SELECT
  t.name                            AS topic,
  array_length(t.partitions)         AS partitions
FROM (
  SELECT unnest(topics) AS t
  FROM tributary_metadata("bootstrap.servers" := 'kafka:9092')
)
ORDER BY partitions DESC;

name: tributary_version
description: Returns the loaded Tributary extension version as a date-stamped build string (e.g. `'20250612.01'`). Use to confirm what's loaded when matching against bug reports or release notes.
